 In
preparing its consolidated financial information, ORIX Corporation (the “Company”) and its subsidiaries have complied with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America. 
 This document may contain forward-looking statements about expected future events and financial results that involve risks and
uncertainties. Such statements are based on the Company’s current expectations and are subject to uncertainties and risks that could cause actual results to differ materially from those described in the forward-looking statements. Factors that
could cause such a difference include, but are not limited to, those described under “Risk Factors” in the Company’s most recent annual report on Form 20-F filed with the U.S. Securities and
Exchange Commission. 
 The Company believes that it may have been a “passive foreign investment company” for U.S.
federal income tax purposes in the year to which these consolidated financial results relate by reason of the composition of its assets and the nature of its income. In addition, the Company may be a PFIC for the foreseeable future. Assuming that
the Company is a PFIC, a U.S. holder of the shares or American depositary shares of the Company will be subject to special rules generally intended to eliminate any benefits from the deferral of U.S. federal income tax that a holder could derive
from investing in a foreign corporation that does not distribute all of its earnings on a current basis. Investors should consult their tax advisors with respect to such rules, which are summarized in the Company’s annual report.

 For the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, after-tax gains or losses arising from
the sale and valuation of shares of Kioxia Holdings Corporation (Head office: Minato-ku, Tokyo; President and CEO: Hiroo Ota; “Kioxia”), recognized through TB Investment Limited Partnership, an
equity-method affiliate of ORIX Corporation, in connection with transactions by Toshiba Corporation (Head office: Kawasaki City, Kanagawa Prefecture; President and CEO: Taro Shimada; “Toshiba”), are recognized in ORIX Corporation’s
consolidated earnings. Although such gains or losses are substantial, such valuation gains or losses are expected to fluctuate with future changes in Kioxia’s share price and therefore remain uncertain. In addition, ORIX Corporation will not
directly receive cash inflows corresponding to such gains or losses. 
 Accordingly, ORIX Corporation’s dividend policy
for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027 is that the annual dividend will be the higher of either an amount calculated by applying 39% to adjusted EPS calculated based on adjusted net income attributable to ORIX Corporation Shareholders
excluding such gains or losses on an after-tax basis, or ¥156.10 per share. Based on this policy, the dividend for the second quarter-end was calculated based on
adjusted EPS for the six months ended September 30, 2026, and the dividend per share was set at ¥113.56 per share, calculated by applying 39% to adjusted EPS based on adjusted net income attributable to ORIX Corporation Shareholders of
¥317,529 million after deducting the after-tax amount of such gains of ¥538,689 million from net income attributable to ORIX Corporation Shareholders of ¥856,218 million for the six
months ended September 30, 2026.

 Overview of Business Performance (April 1, 2026 to September 30, 2026) 
 Total revenues for the six months ended September 30, 2026 increased 10% to ¥1,673,875 million compared to
¥1,527,599 million during the same period of the previous fiscal year primarily due to increases in gains on investment securities and dividends, service income, and sales of goods and real estate. 
 Total expenses increased 11% to ¥1,434,355 million compared to ¥1,297,175 million during the same period of the previous
fiscal year primarily due to increases in selling, general and administrative expenses and costs of goods and real estate sold. 
 Equity in
net income of equity method investments was ¥809,610 million, primarily due to increased equity in net income from a certain equity method investee, partially offset by impairment of certain equity method investments. Gains on sales of
subsidiaries and equity method investments and liquidation losses, net decreased 30% to ¥68,750 million compared to the same period of the previous fiscal year. 
 Due to the above results, income from continuing operations before income taxes for the six months ended September 30, 2026 increased
195% to ¥1,117,880 million compared to ¥378,951 million during the same period of the previous fiscal year and net income attributable to ORIX Corporation Shareholders increased 216% to ¥856,218 million compared to
¥271,096 million during the same period of the previous fiscal year. 
 - 4 - 
 Segment Information 
 Total segment profits for the six months ended September 30, 2026 increased 188% to ¥1,147,389 million compared to the same
period of the previous fiscal year. 
 Beginning with the current consolidated fiscal year, the Company has reorganized its reportable
segments into Japan & APAC, Infrastructure, USA & Europe, and Insurance, reflecting changes in the segments used by the CODM for resource allocation and performance evaluation purposes. For details of the businesses of each
segment, please refer to Note (7), “Segment Information (Unaudited),” under “2. Financial Information.” 
 On
April 27, 2026, the Company decided to sell all shares in ORIX Bank, a consolidated subsidiary, to Daiwa Next Bank, Ltd. As a result of this decision, the operations of ORIX Bank, which had previously been reported as continuing operations,
have been classified as discontinued operations in the current fiscal year in accordance with ASC 205-20 (“Presentation of Financial Statements – Discontinued Operations”). Segment
information presents amounts relating only to continuing operations and excludes the discontinued operations. For further information on the discontinued operations, see Note (8), “Discontinued Operations Information (Unaudited),” under
“2. Financial information.” 
 In connection with these changes, the segment information for the previous interim consolidated
period and as of the end of the previous fiscal year has been retrospectively recast.

 (7) Segment Information (Unaudited) 
 The Group CEO, as the Chief Operating Decision Maker (“CODM”), regularly allocates management resources and assesses segment
performance by using the amount equivalent to income before income taxes attributable to ORIX Corporation Shareholders of each business segment. 
 Beginning with the current consolidated fiscal year, the Company has reorganized its reportable segments into Japan & APAC,
Infrastructure, USA & Europe, and Insurance, reflecting changes in the segments used by the CODM for resource allocation and performance evaluation purposes. In connection with this change, segment information for the previous interim
consolidated period and as of the end of the previous fiscal year has been retrospectively recast. 
 The principal businesses of each segment are as
follows 
 Japan & APAC: 
 The Japan & APAC segment provides business solutions to corporate clients and engages in corporate investment activities in Japan,
Asia and Australia. Its principal businesses include financial services such as leasing, lending and various types of financing; services such as life insurance sales, real estate brokerage and M&A advisory; automobile leasing and fleet
management; rental of electronic measuring instruments, ICT-related equipment, transformers and other equipment; and corporate investments in Japan and overseas. 
 Infrastructure: 
 The
Infrastructure segment engages in the development and operation of assets that support social and industrial infrastructure, as well as the provision of related services. Its principal businesses include environmental and energy-related businesses
such as renewable energy power generation, electricity retailing and waste management; real estate investment and asset management; housing-related businesses; operation of hotels, Japanese inns and other facilities; and operation of airports and
other public infrastructure. The segment also engages in investment, asset management and brokerage businesses related to aircraft and ships. 
 USA & Europe: 
 The
USA & Europe segment engages primarily in investment, financing, asset management and advisory businesses in the United States and Europe.Its principal businesses include investment and financial services such as corporate finance, real
estate finance, real estate investment, debt investment, asset valuation and private equity investment, as well as asset management businesses covering equities, fixed income and other asset classes. 
 Insurance: 
 The Insurance
segment engages in the development and sale of insurance products and asset management activities. 
 - 13 - 
 The accounting policies of the segments are almost the same as accounting policies for
condensed consolidated financial statements except for the treatment of income tax expenses, net income attributable to noncontrolling interests, and net income attributable to redeemable noncontrolling interests. The CODM evaluates segment
performance based on the amount equivalent to income before income taxes attributable to ORIX Corporation Shareholders. Therefore, net income attributable to noncontrolling interests, net income attributable to redeemable noncontrolling interests,
and income tax expenses are not included in segment profit or loss. Most of selling, general and administrative expenses, including compensation costs that are directly related to the revenue generating activities of each segment and excluding the
expenses that should be borne by ORIX Group as a whole, have been accumulated by and charged to each segment. Gains and losses that management does not consider for evaluating the performance of the segments, such as certain interest expenses and
certain foreign exchange gains or losses (included in other (income) and expense) are excluded from the segment profits or losses, and are regarded as corporate items. 
 Assets attributed to each segment are total assets except for certain cash and head office assets. 
 Effective from the current fiscal year, the Company has revised the method of allocating interest expense for certain transactions.
Accordingly, segment figures for the prior interim period have been recast to conform to the current presentation. 
 On April 27,
2026, the Company decided to sell all shares in ORIX Bank, a consolidated subsidiary, to Daiwa Next Bank, Ltd. As a result of this decision, the operations of ORIX Bank, which had previously been reported as continuing operations, have been
classified as discontinued operations in the current fiscal year in accordance with ASC 205-20 (“Presentation of Financial Statements – Discontinued Operations”). Segment information includes
only amounts related to continuing operations and excludes the discontinued operations. Segment information for the previous interim consolidated period and as of the end of the previous fiscal year has also been recast to reflect this change. For
further information on the discontinued operations, see Note (8), “Discontinued Operations Information (Unaudited).”

 (8) Discontinued Operations Information (Unaudited) 
 On April 27, 2026, the Company entered into a share transfer agreement with Daiwa Next Bank, Ltd. to sell all shares in ORIX Bank, a
consolidated subsidiary of the Company. Pursuant to this agreement, the sale of the shares was completed on August 3, 2026. As a result, starting from the second quarter of the current fiscal year, ORIX Bank was excluded from the
Company’s scope of consolidation. 
 As a result of the decision to sell the shares, in accordance with ASC 205-20 (“Presentation of Financial Statements – Discontinued Operations”), the business of ORIX Bank has been classified as held for sale and a discontinued operation. 
 Accordingly, in the condensed consolidated balance sheets, the prior-period balances of the assets and liabilities related to the business of
ORIX Bank have been retrospectively reclassified and presented separately as “Assets of Discontinued Operations Held for Sale” and “Liabilities of Discontinued Operations Held for Sale,” respectively. Furthermore, in the
condensed consolidated statements of income, the results of operations of ORIX Bank are presented separately from continuing operations as “discontinued operations.”. The prior-period results of operations related to the business of ORIX
Bank have also been retrospectively reclassified to conform to the current-period presentation. 
 The Company recognized a gain of
¥124,295 million on the sale of the shares of ORIX Bank on August 3, 2026 in income from discontinued operations before income taxes during the six months ended September 30, 2026.

 (Reference) ORIX Corporation’s dividend policy for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027 
 For the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, after-tax income arising from gains or losses on the
sale and valuation of shares of Kioxia by Toshiba, recognized through TB Investment Limited Partnership, an equity-method affiliate of ORIX Corporation (the “Relevant Gains or Losses”), is recognized in ORIX Corporation’s
consolidated earnings. Although the Relevant Gains or Losses are substantial, they may fluctuate with future changes in Kioxia’s share price. In addition, ORIX Corporation will not directly receive cash inflows corresponding to the Relevant
Gains or Losses. 
 Accordingly, ORIX Corporation’s dividend policy for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027 is that the annual
dividend will be the higher of either an amount calculated by applying 39% to adjusted EPS calculated based on adjusted net income attributable to ORIX Corporation Shareholders after deducting the after-tax 
equivalent of the Relevant Gains or Losses from net income attributable to ORIX Corporation Shareholders, or 156.10 yen per share.
